```{r}
library(simr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(dplyr)
library(ggeffects)
```
```{r}
# 1. Load the original dataset (do not duplicate or row-bind)
fullTest <- read.csv("~/Documents/GitHub/SelfAnchoring/Study 1/Cleaning/output/fullTest.csv")

# 2. Pre-process and scale variables (subsetting to complete cases early saves memory)
fullTest <- fullTest[!is.na(fullTest$predicted) & !is.na(fullTest$ingChoiceN), ]

fullTest$predicted.Z <- scale(fullTest$predicted)
fullTest$ingChoiceN <- as.factor(fullTest$ingChoiceN)
fullTest$subID <- as.factor(fullTest$subID)
fullTest$trait <- as.factor(fullTest$trait)

# 3. Randomly assign subjects to 1 of 3 conditions
set.seed(42) # Ensure reproducible random assignment
unique_subs <- data.frame(subID = unique(fullTest$subID))

# Sample conditions 0, 1, and 2 evenly across the unique subjects
unique_subs$condition <- sample(0:2, size = nrow(unique_subs), replace = TRUE)
unique_subs$condition <- as.factor(unique_subs$condition)

# 4. Join the randomly assigned condition back to the main dataframe
fullTestC <- fullTest %>%
  left_join(unique_subs, by = "subID")

# 5. Fit the initial dummy model on the actual sample size
# Note: Because condition is randomly assigned, the initial empirical estimate 
# for the condition main effect and interaction will be near zero.
m <- glmer(
  ingChoiceN ~ predicted.Z * condition + (predicted.Z | subID) + (1 | trait), 
  data = fullTestC, 
  family = binomial, 
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)),
  nAGQ = 1
)

# Set baseline probability to 50%
fixef(m)["(Intercept)"] <- 0 
fixef(m)["predicted.Z"] <- 0.5
fixef(m)["condition1"] <- 0.01
fixef(m)["condition2"] <- -0.01
fixef(m)["predicted.Z:condition1"] <- -0.35
fixef(m)["predicted.Z:condition2"] <- 0.35

# 7. Extend the model to your target total N 
# If you want 1000 subjects total across all 3 conditions, n=1000 is correct.
m2 <- extend(m, along = "subID", n = 1000)

# 8. Run the power curve
between.power.curve <- powerCurve(
  m2, 
  test = fixed("predicted.Z:condition1", "z"), 
  along = "subID",
  nsim = 100, 
  breaks = c(50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200, 225)
)

# Plot the curve
plot(between.power.curve)
```
